text: . The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has completed ten years of transforming digital payments and has emerged as the backbone of India’s digital payments ecosystem. The UPI, which was launched on 25th August 2016, has surged almost 13 thousand fold in transaction volume. The Finance Ministry said that the annual transaction volume expanded from just 1.78 crore transactions in 2016-17 to over 24 thousand 162 crore transactions in 2025-26. The transaction value also rose sharply from seven thousand crore to nearly 314 lakh crore during the same time period. The Ministry said that UPI has also emerged as a global platform for cross-border digital payments and is currently operational in 11 countries. These are United Arab Emirates, France, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Singapore, Mauritius, Qatar, Cambodia, Greece and Maldives.UPI has emerged as one of the most successful pillars of India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, providing an interoperable, real-time payments platform. Today, it is the preferred mode of payment for millions of users, transforming the way India transacts. By bridging the digital divide, advancing financial inclusion, and expanding access to digital financial services, UPI has empowered individuals and communities across the country while driving broad-based economic participation. The unprecedented scale and reliability achieved by UPI have received global recognition. It said, the International Monetary Fund has acknowledged it as the world’s largest real‑time payment system. As of 2025, UPI accounts for nearly 49 per cent of the world’s real-time payment transaction volume.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 1.3 per cent down at 1,51,184 per 10 grams. Meanwhile, Silver fell 0.9 per cent to 2,28,396 rupees per kilogram.

In Men’s Cricket, India’s 15-member squad for the upcoming three-match T20 International series against Afghanistan has been announced.Shreyas Iyer will lead the Indian side, with Tilak Varma as vice-captain. Ace seamer Jasprit Bumrah returns to the squad, subject to fitness clearance, along with Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar and Harshit Rana. Bumrah missed India’s recent assignments after suffering a knee injury during the ODI series in England in July. He also missed the two-Test series in Sri Lanka.The series will be played at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on the 13th, 15th and 17th of this month. Afghanistan will be the designated host for the series.The Indian top order features a mix of experienced campaigners and young talent, including Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson and Ishan Kishan.The middle order features the likes of skipper Shreyas Iyer, vice-captain Tilak Varma and Shivam Dube. India have opted for three all-round options in Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel and Washington Sundar, while Varun Chakaravarthy will lead the spin attack alongside Ravi Bishnoi.The pace attack will be spearheaded by Jasprit Bumrah and Arshdeep Singh, with Harshit Rana providing an additional option with his effective cutters.The squad largely mirrors India’s team for the upcoming Asian Games to being at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan from 19th of this month.
. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by three paise to close at 94. 98 rupees against the US dollar.

. In Women’s Cricket, India will take on Hong Kong in their second Group A match in the T-20 Asia Cup at Dubai International Stadium in UAE today.The match will begin at 8 PM Indian Standard Time. The Women in Blue opened their campaign with a convincing 94-run win over Thailand in Dubai on Sunday.A victory over Hong Kong will help the Harmanpreet Kaur-led side secure a place in the semifinals of the ongoing eight-team tournament.Last night, Sri Lanka defeated Indonesia by 75 runs in the Group ‘B’ match in Dubai. After posting 124 for the loss of seven wickets in the stipulated 20 overs, Sri Lanka bowled Indonesia out for just 49 runs in 18.3 overs.Earlier, Indonesian women won the toss and opted to bowl. For Sri Lanka, Chamari Athapaththu was declared Player of the Match, who took seven wickets.

The death toll from the devastating Nepal-Tibet flash floods has surged to 1,250, as rescuers battled rain and debris to trace those believed to be trapped in the tunnels along the course of the Bhotekoshi river and underground powerhouses in the Himalayan nation.Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the disaster’s link to climate change must be strongly raised with the international community, as symbolic funerals were held by families of locals still missing after last week’s flash floods. Among the missing people, 583 are foreigners.The joint forces of security personnel, including the Nepal Army, have so far rescued 11,993 people using helicopters and land routes. Around 21,314 security personnel have been mobilised for the search and rescue operations.On the Chinese side, the death toll in the flash flood that struck Gyirong county in Tibet near the Nepal border has increased to 21, with 541 others still missing.Addressing the House of Representatives, Prime Minister  Shah said the scale and nature of the disaster raised serious questions about the growing risks faced by people living in the Himalayan region due to climate change.International development partners, including the Asian Development Bank, World Bank, European Union and United Nations, have also pledged support, while expert teams from India, China and South Korea are being mobilised for rescue operations at hydropower sites.

. The 11 rescue experts who reached Nepal from India today have moved close to Trishuli Bazaar along with specialized equipment. The External Affairs Ministry said in a statement that they are expected to commence their work from tomorrow in coordination with the Nepali Army.India continues to offer rescue and relief assistance to Nepal, with a fifth Indian Air Force flight carrying humanitarian assistance reaching Kathmandu today. It carried about 5.5 tonnes of medical supplies, including antibiotics, analgesics, surgical items and other essential medicines. This flight also carried the 11-member specialized team with more than 6 tonnes of rescue equipment. External Affairs Ministry said that with the latest tranche of assistance, India has delivered around 74 tonnes of relief assistance to Nepal to date.Rescue operations in the wake of devastating floods in Nepal have continued. So far, 166 Indian nationals have been rescued, including three individuals today. A total of 410 Indian nationals who were visiting Tibet Autonomous Region for pilgrimage or other activities have left China today.The Ministry informed that the Indian tunnel rescue team moved its base to Syabrubesi from Trishuli, which will help reduce the time taken to travel to Chilime, where the rescue operations are taking place. The team continued its search operations in Chilime in collaboration with the Nepali Army. Amidst deep slush and blockages inside the tunnel, the team was able to move forward by about 100 metres today. To ensure expedited progress, the possibility of an improvised road approach to the tunnel was explored so that more heavy equipment could be used for search and rescue.Meanwhile, the forensics team from India is now working in two laboratories in Kathmandu for the examination and analysis of DNA samples in collaboration with experts from Nepal.

. A 19-member Indian forensic team has begun analysing DNA samples alongside forensic experts to assist in identifying people affected by the recent flash floods in Nepal. The Indian Embassy said that the team commenced the analysis at the Nepal Police Central Forensic Science Laboratory and the National Forensic Science Laboratory in the Khumaltar area of Kathmandu Valley.The Indian experts are working with their counterparts to speed up the processing of DNA samples collected from flood-affected areas and help establish the identities of victims and missing persons. The deployment of Indian forensic team is part of ongoing efforts to support Nepal in the aftermath of the recent flash floods, which caused significant loss of life and left several people unaccounted for.Nepal Police said 1,068 bodies have been recovered by yesterday evening, of which 400 had only partial remains, complicating the identification process. With the death toll continuing to rise following last week’s deadly floods, authorities have collected DNA samples from several unclaimed bodies to support identification efforts in the future.Chitwan district has reported the highest number of recovered bodies so far. Authorities have buried hundreds of bodies in open spaces along riverbanks after collecting DNA samples for future identification. According to Nepal Police, 4,606 people remain unaccounted for, including 583 foreigners, raising concerns that the death toll could increase further. Authorities said efforts are continuing to trace people who remain unaccounted for at various hydropower projects along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river corridors in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts.

. The Ebola outbreak in Congo has claimed the lives of more than three thousand people out of over 6,100 confirmed cases. According to the latest government data released today, the outbreak has recorded 6,186 confirmed cases, including 3,007 deaths, since it was declared in mid-May. It is now the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record.The disease is spreading rapidly for several reasons, including conflict in the country’s eastern region, where the outbreak is concentrated, attacks on health workers, the movement of miners, and inadequate health infrastructure. The reopening of schools during the outbreak has also raised concerns about the spread of the virus in classrooms.The World Health Organization (WHO) has warned that the outbreak could surpass the deadliest Ebola outbreak on record-the West African outbreak between 2014 and 2016, which killed around 11,000 people. There is currently no vaccine or approved treatment specifically for the rare Bundibugyo virus strain responsible for the current outbreak.The government is, however, distributing the Ervebo vaccine, which has been used to help control previous Ebola outbreaks. The WHO says the vaccine could offer some protection. The virus has now spread to six provinces in Congo.

. Japan Credit Rating Agency (JCR) has upgraded India’s Long-Term Foreign Currency and Local Currency Issuer Ratings by one notch from ‘BBB+’ to ‘A-’, while maintaining the Stable Outlook. JCR has also raised India’s country ceiling by one notch to ‘A’.The Finance Ministry said that the upgrade reflects India’s solid economic growth, the effectiveness of economic policies in strengthening the foundations for growth, and the improved soundness of the financial system.The Ministry said that the upgrade comes against the backdrop of a challenging global environment and underscores the continued strengthening of India’s economic fundamentals, supported by sustained growth, effective economic policies, improved fiscal quality and a stronger financial system.In a statement, JCR noted that the Indian economy has maintained a high growth rate, supported by robust private consumption and public investment.The agency also highlighted the Indian Government’s continued implementation of policies, including the development of digital public infrastructure and the implementation of the Goods and Services Tax, which have strengthened India’s economic foundations.The agency also recognised the improvement in the quality of fiscal expenditure, with greater emphasis on capital expenditure, particularly infrastructure investment. JCR noted that the Central Government’s fiscal deficit declined from 4.7 percent in Financial Year 25 to 4.4 percent in Financial Year 26, while capital expenditure remained high.

. Iran today warned that it would adopt a new strategy in its ongoing conflict with the United States following the latest escalation between the two sides. In a social media post, Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Iran’s new strategy on the battlefield, in diplomacy and in countering the economic blockade would shatter the foundations of its adversaries.The warning came after a fresh wave of Iranian attacks on US positions across West Asia, in what was described as the heaviest exchange between the two sides in weeks.Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said its forces targeted US bases in Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Bahrain and Iraq’s autonomous Kurdistan region. The strikes followed US military operations against Iranian targets, which Tehran said killed 18 people.The renewed hostilities have further complicated diplomatic efforts to resolve the six-month-old conflict. Iran continues to put pressure on the strategically important Strait of Hormuz, while the United States is pursuing a counter-blockade targeting Iranian ports.Meanwhile, Iran’s Foreign Ministry accused the United States of committing a war crime following a deadly strike on a wedding ceremony in the southern Iranian city of Sirik.US Central Command said the US military never targets civilians, in contrast to Iran, while not directly addressing the reported strike on the wedding venue.The latest escalation began after Washington launched strikes on Iranian assets on Sunday. The United States said the attacks were carried out in retaliation for Iran’s alleged efforts to lay mines in the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on US personnel.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called for sensitising Urban Local Bodies to the challenges arising from urbanisation, including population growth and future water requirements, and suggested organising similar Chintan Shivirs for Urban Local Bodies. Mr Modi today chaired the valedictory session of the two-day National Departmental Summit on Water, organised by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. He called for greater adoption of water-saving technologies. He also suggested dedicated exhibitions and workshops, including exposure to global best practices, to enable Indian manufacturers and stakeholders to develop and scale efficient solutions.The prime minister appreciated the intensive two-day deliberations and emphasised that the actionable and time-bound action points emerging from the Summit should be pursued through a continuous process of review and learning. He suggested that the Summit should not remain a one-time exercise and called for a continuous process of review and follow-up.Emphasising Jan Bhagidari, Mr Modi suggested promoting “Jal Utsav” to create greater awareness among people. Prime Minister called for making de-silting a regular programme and developing clear criteria and SOPs for de-silting. On dam safety, he stressed rigorous preparedness before every monsoon, adherence to prescribed precautions and creating awareness among school students, including through suitable incorporation in educational curricula.The prime minister further called for strengthening knowledge and capacity on water management and governance in universities and higher educational institutions. He suggested structured inter-State study-visits involving public representatives, officials and farmers to facilitate practical learning and replication of successful interventions.The prime minister called for robust water data governance, with water-sector data brought together, systematically managed, analysed and effectively utilised. He recommended the use of AI for data collection and analysis through a uniform format. He also stressed anticipatory and integrated planning to address water scarcity through suitable utilisation of treated water for agriculture and industrial purposes.

. Indian table tennis player Ankur Bhattacharjee has won his maiden WTT men’s singles title at the WTT Feeder Olomouc tournament in Czechia. He also secured the men’s doubles gold with fellow Indian Akash Pal. World number 78 defeated third seed Slovenia’s Deni Kozul 3-1 in the singles final to complete a memorable campaign. Earlier, Ankur and Akash Pal defeated Hungary’s Csaba Andras Szantosi and Poland’s Alan Kulczycki Zalewski 3-1 in the men’s doubles final.Ankur, who was a finalist at the Europe Youth Smash in Sweden in 2025, had already reached two quarterfinals and two semifinals in 2026 before claiming his maiden WTT title in Olomouc.

The government has extended the last date for submission of applications by selected meritorious students for National Means cum Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for 2026-27 to 30th September this year. The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). Following the extension, the last date for Level-1 verification at the Institute Nodal Officer is 15th October while the last date for Level-2 verification with the District Nodal Officer is 31st October.The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level that is Class eight and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level that is Class 12. The scholarship amount is 12 thousand rupees per annum per student.The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class 9 students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State and UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes 10 to 12 based on the student’s academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools.The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than 3.50 lakh rupees per annum, a minimum of 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in the Class 8 examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship. The government has advised all the eligible students to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal within the extended timeline.

In Badminton, India’s Unnati Hooda has made an early exit from the China Masters Super 750 tournament in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.World No. 25 Hooda lost to South Korea’s World No. 12 Kim Ga-eun in straight games, 10-21, 18-21, in the opening round of the women’s singles.Earlier, India’s Men’s Doubles pair of Hariharan Amsakarunan and M R Arjun retired at the first-game interval in their opening-round match. The Indian duo were trailing China’s Chen Bo Yang and Liu Yi, 8-11 when they decided to concede the match.The focus now shifts tothe remaining Indian players. Several leading shuttlers will begin their campaigns tomorrow. Lakshya Sen, Kidambi Srikanth and Tanvi Sharma will be in action. Devika Sihag will also take the court. The top-seeded Men’s Doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will lead India’s challenge at the tournament.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended around half a per cent lower today, extending their losing streak to three consecutive sessions. The Sensex declined 374 points to close at 76,570, while the Nifty fell 141 points to settle at 23,914. In the broader market, the Nifty Midcap 100 index slipped half a per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 index declined 0.4 per cent. Elevated crude oil prices, rising global bond yields and future inflation concerns dented Dalal Street sentiment.Earlier, the markets opened with a gap down amid negative global cues. Both indices traded within a narrow range and remained under pressure throughout the day. However, they pared some of their losses after the closing auction session.In the Sensex pack, 20 out of 30 companies logged losses. Among the top laggards, Asian Paints, HDFC Bank, Mahindra and Mahindra declined 1.6 per cent, HCL Tech dropped one and a half per cent and Bharat Electronics Limited lost 1.3 per cent. In contrast, Adani Ports climbed 1.6 per cent, Bajaj Finance, PowerGrid, NTPC gained one per cent and Titan added 0.7 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 18 out of 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top underperformers, Auto declined 1.7 per cent, IT declined 1.2 per cent and Insurance as well as Capital Goods dipped 1.1 per cent. In contrast, Utilities rose 1.4 per cent, Housing Finance as well as Energy gained 0.7 per cent and Power added half a per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2560 companies declined, 1799 advanced and 217 remained unchanged.

. World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka brushed aside Colombia’s Camila Osorio 6-2, 6-4 in the first round of the US Open at Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York. Top seed Sabalenka’s second-round clash is against Russia’s Polina Iatcenko as she looks to become only the third woman after Serena Williams and Chris Evert to win three straight US Opens. The Belarusian hit 32 winners against Osorio in a match which lasted an hour and 27 minutes. Osorio handed Sabalenka a break with a ⁠double fault in the third game – one of five she had across the opening set – and slipped 4-1 ‌behind as the Belarusian converted on another break point with an unreturnable backhand.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) today said its special US dollar-Indian rupee (USD-INR) forex swap facility has received forex inflows of over 136 billion US dollars till August 31, 2026. Of the total inflows, Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) [FCNR-B] deposits accounted for the overwhelming majority, amounting to 127.2 billion US dollars. Meanwhile, Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs) brought in 5.26 billion US dollars and External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) contributed 3.89 billion US dollars.The Reserve Bank introduced the special USD-INR forex swap facility covering FCNR(B) deposits, ECBs and OFCBs inflows on June 8, 2026. The swap facility, announced to boost the inflow of dollars amid a weakening rupee, was originally available until the end of September, but it was shortened by a month due to the encouraging response to the facility. The scheme has now been closed for FCNR(B) deposits, while the facility for ECBs and OFCBs remains available until December 31, 2026.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today paid tributes to legendary actor and filmmaker Uttam Kumar on his birth centenary.In a social media post, Mr Modi described Mahanayak Uttam Kumar as a legend whose timeless performances continue to connect with audiences across generations.The Prime Minister also shared a segment of his remarks on Uttam Kumar from the latest episode of his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ programme broadcast on Akashvani last Sunday.

. Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football, bringing an end to a 20-year Argentina career that included a World Cup triumph, two Copa América titles and a record 207 appearances for his country. Messi said the decision had been on his mind since the World Cup final defeat to Spain, before the death of his father further convinced him it was time to step away. The 39-year-old revealed the decision in a statement posted on his official Instagram account, confirming that he would no longer wear the Argentina jersey after one of the most celebrated international careers in football history.Messi said the decision had been painful, particularly because of the emotional bond he has shared with the national team and Argentina’s supporters throughout his career. He led his country to the World Cup title in 2022 after years of near misses and also helped Argentina win two Copa América crowns. His international journey also included World Cup final defeats in 2014 and again this summer, with the loss to Spain in July proving to be a significant moment in his decision-making process.

. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that he had carved out a unique place for himself in the field of Gujarati music, carrying forward the rich musical tradition of his father Avinash Vyas.Mr Modi added that the demise of Gaurang Vyas leaves Gujarat feeling the loss of a talented creator and said that his invaluable contribution to the Gujarati music scene will always be remembered.

. The US has begun fresh strikes on Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets inside Iran. Iranian media reported that explosions were heard in Bandar Abbas, Hormuz, Asaluyeh, Jiroft, Qeshm Island, Konarak, Chabahar, Jask, Sirik and Lavan.US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it completed the wave of strikes against Iranian military targets, which included air defence sites, mine-laying capabilities, and communications sites, among others. It said that the strikes follow recent attempted attacks by IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members. Iran’s Foreign Ministry said that the US strikes hit a home hosting a wedding ceremony in the city of Kuhestak, resulting in the deaths of four civilians and over 50 injuries.US President Donald Trump, in a post on Truth Social, has warned that any retaliation by Iran against the very justified attack will see a stronger response by Washington. Trump also hinted that a much bigger attack against Tehran is yet to come.In response, Iran’s IRGC claimed an attack on US military barracks at Jordan’s Camp Titin. Iran’s army said it targeted US forces stationed at Bahrain’s Sheikh Isa airbase. Kuwait’s army said the country’s air defences responded to attacks by “hostile drones” from Iran.

. Government has notified the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026. The move marks a significant step towards establishing Indian Standard Time (IST) as the common, legally recognised and traceable time reference for the country.The Rules were notified by the Department of Consumer Affairs on the 27th of last month and published in the Official Gazette on the 29th.They provide a comprehensive framework for the generation, maintenance, dissemination and use of IST. The Rules will come into force 180 days from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.The initiative supports the Government’s vision of “One Nation, One Time”, ensuring that critical sectors and digital systems across the country operate with a common and reliable time reference.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, along with other SCO leaders, participated in the official opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, last evening. The biennial event celebrates the rich sporting traditions, culture and heritage of nomadic civilisations, bringing together countries in a vibrant celebration of their shared culture.Earlier, Prime Minister Modi held bilateral meetings with leaders of Russia, Iran, the Kyrgyz Republic and Armenia on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit. The Prime Minister will address the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit today.

. All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi has introduced a new course titled GARBHINI MITRA to Strengthen Ayurveda-Based Maternal Wellness Support for the 2026-2027 academic session.The Ministry of AYUSH said that the six-month course is designed to develop trained personnel to provide appropriate health education, lifestyle guidance, and community-level support to women during pregnancy and the postnatal period.The ministry noted that Candidates of 18 years or above, who have passed the Senior Secondary examination from any recognized board are eligible to apply before its last date that is 31st August.Once completed, candidates can work as Garbhini Mitra Assistants, Prenatal or Postnatal Care Assistants, Antenatal Wellness Guides and Maternal Health Support Workers, across different Ayush centres, maternity clinics and wellness institutions.The course inculcates traditional ayurvedic concepts of Garbhini Paricharya, Sutika Paricharya and Garbhadhana Vidhi.

. ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan has said that the EOS-05 Earth observation satellite will be launched tomorrow. The satellite is scheduled to lift off at 2:55 AM aboard the GSLV-F17 rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota.Mr Narayanan said EOS-05 is a state-of-the-art Earth observation spacecraft and India’s first imaging satellite to be placed in a geosynchronous orbit. He said the mission will further strengthen India’s Earth observation capabilities and improve the delivery of Earth observation services.The ISRO Chairman was speaking to the media after offering prayers at the Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Tirumala yesterday.Before offering prayers, Mr Narayanan placed models of the GSLV-F17 rocket at the feet of Lord Venkateswara. He said all arrangements for the launch have been completed at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota.

. The International Cricket Council today moved the inaugural Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 to India from Sri Lanka. The six-team event will be played in Mumbai and Vadodara from 14th to 28th of February.Sri Lanka was dropped as host as the sport is grappling with governance issues in the island nation, with the ICC Board approving India as the new host.The tournament will bring together six of the world’s leading women’s cricket teams, Australia, England, India, New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka. These six teams have qualified for the tournament as per their positions in the ICC Women’s T20 International Team Rankings on the 6th of July qualification cut-off date. They will compete in a round-robin league, with the top two sides advancing to the final on 28th February.ICC Chairman,Jay Shah, said, the ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 marks an exciting new chapter for women’s cricket. He said, as the inaugural edition of the tournament, it will bring together the best teams in the world in an intense, high-quality competition, while creating even greater incentive for teams to continue rising through the rankings and competing for a place on the global stage.India hosted the Women’s ODI World Cup last year when the home team won a pathbreaking title.

. The Publications Division of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has received seven awards at the Federation of Indian Publishers (FIP) Awards for Excellence in Book Production, 2026. The Division’s journals, books and reference publications in Hindi, English and Urdu have been recognised in various categories.Director General, Publications Division, Dr. Dhiraj Kakadia said that the books and journals published by the Division play an important role in bringing diverse and valuable content related to national development, literature, culture, art and contemporary issues to readers. He said, the seven awards received by the Publications Division are a testament to the collective hard work, dedication and excellence of its officers and personnel.

. In Asian markets today, South Korea’s Kospi gained more than 0.2 per cent while Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped over 0.1 per cent.In European markets, Germany’s DAX was trading 0.9 per cent down, and London’s FTSE 100 dipped over half a per cent, a short while ago.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Prime Minister of Belgium, Bart De Wever, will hold bilateral talks in New Delhi today. Both leaders will discuss the entire spectrum of bilateral relations, as well as regional and global issues of mutual interest.The Belgian Prime Minister arrived in the national capital last night on a three-day visit to India.Belgian Minister of Defence Theo Francken is accompanying Prime Minister De Wever. This is his first visit to India since taking office in February last year. The visiting dignitary will also deliver a keynote address at a Confederation of Indian Industry business event, in the context of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement.Akashvani correspondent reports that the visit will provide an opportunity to further strengthen the India-Belgium partnership and advance cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, defence and security, and renewable energy.India and Belgium share historical ties spanning over three centuries. Belgium was among the first European countries to establish diplomatic relations with independent India in September 1947.Belgium is an important economic partner for India in Europe. Bilateral trade reached over 13 billion dollars in 2025-26.Diamond trade, with Antwerp as a major global diamond hub, remains a significant component of bilateral commerce. Belgium is also an important source of investment in India.FDI inflows from Belgium amounted to approximately 4.2 billion dollars between April 2000 and December 2025. Science, technology and Innovation cooperation is an important pillar of the partnership and India and Belgium have developed cooperation in renewable energy, clean technologies and sustainability.Defence cooperation is also emerging as an important new dimension of the partnership, reflecting the diversification of bilateral ties into strategic and security-related areas.Belgium’s appointment of a Defence Attaché in New Delhi reflects this intent of deepening cooperation in defence.The Indian diaspora is an important bridge between the two countries, with around 35 thousand people of Indian origin in Belgium, contributing substantially to economic, social and cultural life in that country.

. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has said that the country today stands as an important place of transformation and renewed confidence, showcasing the results of collective determination and efforts. The Vice President said this after releasing a book titled Sankalp Se Siddhi ka Modi Yug written by Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari. He said that whether it is advancing technology, building modern infrastructure, and strengthening national unity and promoting women-led development, education is the tool for empowerment. Mr Radhakrishnan also highlighted the contributions of the country’s youth, women, farmers, workers, and every citizen for their involvement in building a stronger and prosperous nation. He also underlined that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the only leader in the world to provide free Covid-19 vaccines not only to 140 crore Indian people but also to hundred more countries.Speaking about the book, the Vice President said that through the publication, the author seeks to bring together many aspects of country’s larger narratives, reviving pride in cultural heritage and enhancing the country’s voice at the global stage. He added that the book reflects the journey of the nation and encourages everyone and boosts their enthusiasm.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres will participate in the 18th BRICS Summit later this month in New Delhi. As the chair this year, India will be hosting the 18th BRICS Summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The summit will bring together leaders of BRICS member and partner countries as well as outreach invitees, according to the Ministry of External Affairs.The theme for India’s BRICS chairship is ‘Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability’. India, a founding member of BRICS, has previously held its chairship in 2012, 2016 and 2021. India assumed its fourth BRICS chairship on January 1, 2026. BRICS is celebrating its 20th anniversary this year.

. In Egypt, 22 people were killed and 28 others injured today when a passenger bus crashed in the Sinai Peninsula. The casualties included both Egyptians and Jordanians. Egypt’s Health Ministry said in a statement that the accident took place on a road linking the tourist resorts of Dahab and Nuweiba in South Sinai province. Local media reported that the bus was travelling from Cairo to Amman in Jordan when it overturned on the road between Dahab and Nuweiba. The reports said 10 Jordanians were among those killed in the crash. Some media reports said the bus overturned after one of its tyres burst.

. Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju today held a series of bilateral meetings with leaders from several nations on the sidelines of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) Summit in Serbia’s capital Belgrade. The meetings focused on bolstering bilateral cooperation and broadening engagement across vital sectors.During the diplomatic outreach, Mr Rijiju held discussions with Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, Waleed A. M. Elkhereiji. They deliberated on ways to intensify the robust and historic ties between New Delhi and Riyadh while exploring pathways to expand collaboration in domains of shared concern.The Union Minister also met President of the Serbian National Assembly, Ana Brnabic. Both sides deliberated on the enduring connection between India and Serbia, alongside the significance of legislative diplomacy in bridging the two nations and their populations. Furthermore, he met Serbian Minister of Internal and Foreign Trade, Jagoda Lazarevic, to review opportunities for scaling up commercial and economic ties while forging fresh pathways for joint growth.Mr Rijiju also held talks with Angola’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Tete Antonio, with a focus on strengthening the bilateral alliance and widening cooperation for mutual prosperity.Yesterday, the Union Minister called on President of Serbia, Aleksandar Vucic, reaffirming the firm friendship and expanding partnership underpinned by mutual regard and collective priorities.

. Global crude oil prices fell today. Brent crude was trading one per cent down at 93 US dollars and 73 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was also trading one per cent lower at 89 US dollars and 24 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. In Badminton, India’s Kidambi Srikanth and Tanvi Sharma advanced to second round of China Masters Super 750 tournament with straight-game victories in respective Singles’ events in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province. Men’s Doubles duo, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, and the mixed doubles pair, Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto also moved to the next round.In Men’s Singles, 2021 world championships silver-medallist, Srikanth defeated Chinese Taipei’s Chi Yu Jen 21-16, 21-15 in the opening match. The former World Number One will next face World Number 9 Victor Lai of Canada.However, Lakshya Sen, a 2021 world championships bronze-medallist, was knocked out of the tournament after going down against Victor Lai, 14-21, 7-21.In Women’s Singles, Tanvi overpowered Denmark’s Amalie Schulz 21-16, 21-17. The 17-year-old from Punjab, who won her maiden BWF World Tour title at the Taipei Open last month, will face Japan’s Tomoka Miyazaki in next round.In Men’s Doubles, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty registered a 21-11, 21-16 win over Malaysia’s Junaidi Arif and Kang Khai Xing. The Asian Games gold medallist pair will next take on the Popov brothers, Christo and Toma Junior of France.Mixed Doubles pair of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto defeated Thailand’s Tonnakorn Saeheng and Tonnicha Saeheng 21-8, 21-9. The duo will meet Chinese Taipei’s Liu Kuang Heng and Hsu Yin-Hui next.

Union Minister for Education Pralhad Joshi held a meeting with the Secretary, Department of School Education and Literacy, in New Delhi, to discuss the next phase of school education reforms.In a social media post yesterday, Mr Joshi said that the discussions focused on strengthening the foundations of learning, promoting innovation in classrooms and ensuring that the education system keeps pace with the aspirations of a young and dynamic India.The Union Minister also held a meeting with the Secretary, Department of Higher Education, to review the preparedness for the future examinations scheduled in the upcoming months. Senior Officials of the National Testing Agency were also present during the discussion.

The Government said that the country has adequate availability of onion and it has begun a calibrated and targeted release of buffer stocks through Kanda Express and road transport to ensure moderation of seasonal price pressures. The Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Ministry said that retail intervention efforts have expanded significantly across 19 cities, supported by the dispatch of over 30 trucks to ensure widespread availability.The Ministry has informed that two Kanda Express consignments have been dispatched from Nashik as part of this initiative. It added that the first rake, carrying 450 Metric Tonnes of onions, reached Delhi and was subsequently distributed across Varanasi, Lucknow, Chandigarh and Amritsar and across the Delhi-NCR region. The Ministry further said that the second rake, carrying 840 MT of onions, reached Chennai yesterday and is likely to be distributed across various districts of Tamil Nadu. The Ministry noted that around one thousand Metric Tonnes of onions are being transported by road to major consumption centres, based on prevailing market conditions and price trends.The Ministry has informed 210 crore rupees have been paid directly to around three thousand 400 farmers, ensuring timely payments. The Government remains committed to supporting onion farmers while ensuring adequate and affordable availability for consumers. The Government has also put in place robust security measures to prevent any leakages and address security concerns during the movement and disposal of large quantities of onions through railway rakes.It highlighted that the release of onions from buffer stocks has improved market availability and prices have shown a decline from the day following the commencement of disposal, with increased supplies expected to further support price stability.

. In Nagaland, the 10th Edition of the Capt (Late) N Kenguruse, Mahavir Chakra Memorial Football Tournament 2026-27 will be held from November 2 to 10. The tournament will be conducted under the aegis of Spear Corps and Headquarters Inspector General Assam Rifles (North), in collaboration with the Nagaland Football Association and supported by the Kohima District Football Association and Chümoukedima District Football Association.A total of 20 teams are expected to participate, divided into four pools of five teams each.  Matches will be played at Indira Gandhi Stadium, Kohima, and Chümoukedima Football Stadium. The tournament carries a total prize pool of 8.69 lakh rupees. Registrations will open today and close at 08:00 PM on 30 September. The tournament will culminate with the closing ceremony on November 10. The milestone edition seeks to celebrate football, inspire young talent and carry forward the values of courage, dedication and sportsmanship associated with the late Captain N. Kenguruse.

. Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah while speaking in Parliament today thanked India for its quick response to the devastating flash floods, as rescue teams continue searching for survivors and missing people in some of the worst-affected areas. The death toll from devastating flash floods in the Himalayan Nation has risen to 1,204, with nearly 4,216 people still missing, as rescuers battled rain and debris to trace those believed to be trapped in the tunnels along the course of the Bhotekoshi river and underground powerhouses.Addressing the House of Representatives, Mr Shah acknowledged the emergency assistance provided by India and China, including relief supplies, technical support and rescue personnel.The Prime Minister said, the devastation caused by the flash floods, stands as a stark warning of escalating climate risks in the Himalayan region and called on the international community to share responsibility for mitigating its impacts. He said, the scale and nature of the disaster raised serious questions about the growing risks faced by people living in the Himalayan region due to climate change. Mr Shah said experts have identified the disaster- one of the largest in the region- as resulting from an avalanche of snow and rock in the high Himalayas. He said, this is a serious signal that, alongside climate change, the risks they must bear in the Himalayan region are increasing. He stressed that Climate change is a product of the whole world’s contribution and mitigating and managing its effects is the shared responsibility of the global community.On rescue and relief operations, Prime Minister Shah said, security agencies have been deployed across the affected areas, while local authorities have urged people to move to safer locations. He said, army helicopters are carrying out rescue and evacuation operations, with private helicopters also on standby if required.The Prime Minister also informed the House that local and provincial authorities are working together to restore electricity, water supplies and transport links in the affected areas.Mr Shah noted that Nepal has already received messages of goodwill and material assistance from multiple countries and multilateral partners, including India, China, the United States, Japan, the Asian Development Bank, the World Bank, the European Union and the United Nations. He informed the House that over 7 billion Nepalese Rupee, has been collected in the Prime Minister’s Relief Fund so far.Rescue teams are also moving families from high-risk areas to safer locations, clearing roads blocked by debris and coordinating relief and search operations with local authorities and residents. However, continuing rain is disrupting search and rescue operations in Rasuwa and Nuwakot.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

The programme will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani and Doordarshan network, the AIR News website, and the Newsonair mobile app. It will also be live-streamed on the YouTube channels of AIR News, DD News, the PMO, and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration’s latest attempt to limit birthright citizenship in the United States.U.S. District Judge Deborah Boardman issued a preliminary injunction after immigrant rights advocates argued that the new order violated the U.S. Constitution.This decision comes shortly after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled on June 30 that Trump’s initial 2025 executive order violated the 14th Amendment, which guarantees citizenship to children born on American soil regardless of their parents’ immigration status.In response to the Supreme Court’s rejection, President Trump signed a revised executive order on August 6 specifically targeting birth tourism and denying citizenship to children of foreign government workers, individuals involved in immigration fraud, or those classified as alien enemies.However, lawyers representing babies affected by the restrictions successfully asked the judge to intervene.Judge Boardman’s new ruling prevents government agencies, including the State Department, Homeland Security, and the Social Security Administration from denying or interfering with the citizenship of these children while the legal challenge continues.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India’s economic growth of 7.8 per cent is a reflection of hard work and collective resolve of 140 crore citizens. Sharing a video in a social media post today, Mr Modi said that India is progressing at a fast pace despite global problems like ongoing wars and instability since the Covid-19 pandemic. He said in order to maintain this growth, it is important to become Atmanirbhar Bharat.The Prime Minister urged the citizens to adopt Swadeshi, promote Vocal for Local and support Made in India products. Mr Modi also urged the citizens to restrict foreign travel, avoid planning weddings in foreign countries and not buy gold if not necessary. Mr Modi expressed confidence that if all the citizens adopt the practice of Swadeshi, the vision of Viksit Bharat will be achieved in 100 years of independence.

Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections in the last month witnessed a significant rise to 1,99,853 crore rupees, marking a 14.8 percent year-on-year increase from 1,74,116 crore rupees in august 2025. According to the provisional data released by the Finance Ministry, Gross domestic GST revenue stood at 1,37,249 crore rupees, up 9.3 per cent from a year ago. GST collections from imports surged 29 per cent to 62,604 crore rupees, providing a boost to the overall monthly mop-up.
